text:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: streaming-decode-p99 > 2.5s in us-west-2 for service=streaming-infer. Recent kernel/compilepath rollout v2.1 at 60% (09:12 UTC). Paging events and tail stalls increasing.

maya (oncall): grabbing it. paging runtime + infra. @sachin @leo can you join?

sachin: seeing it live. p95 jumped 400ms -> ~1.1s; p99 spiked 1.2s -> ~3.2s since ~09:10. KV pagefault / eviction counters up on decode worker threads. Affected routes: streaming-infer.*.

leo: I pulled the rollout notes — v2.1 included TRT 8.2 + flashattn 1.4 + new compile flags. Flags: `-march=sm80 -O3 -funroll-loops -funsafe-math-optimizations`. Suspect aggressive inlining + new linker path is increasing working set and causing more GPU memory churn -> paging tail.

sachin: logs snippet:
```
[09:13:02] runtime.decode: pagefault handle_start kernel=compilepath-v2.1 node=gpu-03
[09:13:03] runtime.kvcache: eviction triggered: userKeys=1200, mem=0.98
[09:13:04] runtime.stream: decode latency=3240ms seq=254
```

infra-sre: can pin pools if needed. We can route traffic away from nodes with v2.1 and bump back to v2.0.

maya (oncall): priority = high. Can we mitigate without full rollback? Any quick toggles?

leo: two quick levers: 1) disable FlashAttention compute path so we use fallback kernels; 2) enable runtime kernel fallback to the non-optimized compilepath. Both are env toggles.

sachin: trying fallback env now on a small subset. Command I'm running:
```
kubectl set env deployment/runtime --containers=runtime \ 
  REDWOOD_RUNTIME_KERNEL_FALLBACK=true -n prod && \
  kubectl set env deployment/runtime --containers=runtime REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FEATURE_FLASHATTN=0 -n prod
```
Applying to deployment streaming-infer-canary (10 pods) first.

infra-sre: applying pool pin for us-west-2-gpu-pool-03 -> pin to compilepath-v2.0. Doing canary rollback: shifting 40% traffic to v2.0 now.

deploy-bot: Rollback action started at 09:24 UTC. Traffic shift: v2.1 60% -> 20%, v2.0 40% -> 80% (canary stage).

sachin: quick metrics update: after toggles on canary nodes p99 on canary dropped from 3.2s -> 720ms in ~3m. Global p99 currently 1.8s (still draining). KV eviction rate on pinned nodes down 70%.

maya (oncall): good. Any customer-facing impact?

sachin: two support tickets from high-traffic customers: acct/acme-enterprises and acct/greenfield-ai reporting streaming stalls and reconnects. Both partial degradation, not full outage. Estimated affected sessions <0.5% of overall.

leo: root cause hypothesis: aggressive compile-time inlining + new TRT kernels increased persistent working set + changed memory access pattern with flashattn; combined with particular batch-size distribution triggers pagefault waterfall on some longer streams. We'll need a compilepath patch to reduce inlining heuristics.

infra-sre: can confirm nodes with v2.1 had GPU memory high watermark ~98% and more pagefaults. Pinned nodes (v2.0) are stable.

maya (oncall): severity = sev2 due to customer impact and SLO breach. Initiating incident channel creation. Incident owner?

amanda: I can take ownership for the remainder of the shift. Summary so far: mitigations applied (kernel fallback + flashattn disabled), canary rollback in progress, p99 trending down. I'll coordinate next steps, postmortem, and customer comms.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-3173 | Priority: P2 | Channel: #incident-6918274000 | Owner: amanda | Started: 2026-03-15T09:28:00Z

sachin: action items for triage:
- capture full decode worker flamegraphs from affected nodes (gcore + nvprof traces)
- capture kvcache usage histograms for last 2 hours
- reproduce locally with workload from acct/acme-enterprises (we have replay)
- run compilepath build with lowered inliner threshold (-finline-limit=1000) for candidate patch

leo: I'll prepare build with inliner reduction and a non-flashattn TRT variant. Want to smoke test on staging with long tail streams (>= 20k tokens).

infra-sre: rolling out fallback to all canary nodes now (applied env to 30 nodes). Watch windows: next 10 mins.

deploy-bot: Notice: traffic shift complete for canary at 09:34 UTC. Monitoring.

sachin: global p99 09:36 UTC -> 680ms; p95 210ms. Paging rate back to baseline. Customer tickets: support flagged both customers as "degraded" but no disconnects in last 5m.

maya (oncall): excellent. Keep collection of artifacts. Amanda, please continue as owner. I'll prepare brief for leadership (impact, mitigation, timeline).

amanda: taking over. Handoff notes: mitigations: kernel fallback + flashattn disabled, canary rollback to v2.0 completed, pinned pools for us-west-2. Immediate impact: p99 reduced from 3.2s -> ~650-700ms; affected customers limited and notified. Next steps: collect traces, test compilepath patch, patch and stage, plan controlled rollout with telemetry gating. I'll own customer comms with support.

amanda: timeline/logs so far:
- 09:12 UTC: compilepath v2.1 rollout (60%)
- 09:16 UTC: p99 spike observed, paging increases
- 09:20 UTC: oncall paged; triage started
- 09:24 UTC: env toggles + canary rollback started
- 09:34 UTC: canary rollback complete; mitigations effective

incident-bot: Next update scheduled in 30m.

maya (oncall): thx everyone. Please add all artifacts to the incident thread and link PRs. We'll do a follow-up postmortem; set severity and blameless notes. :thumbsup:
